title: mavai declarative service-definition file (mavai-services/1)
description: Structural schema for the mavai family's declarative service-definition file. It validates the parsed data model of the YAML document. The canonical specification is the prose format specification maintained in the family's internal requirements catalog (MAVAI-SERVICES-FORMAT.md; amendment session 2026-07-25); this schema is its machine-checkable structural projection and never introduces a rule the specification does not state — $comment fields cite the mandating sections. Semantic obligations the schema cannot express (type-registry resolution, factory-signature configuration validation for user types, duplicate-grid-point refusal, stepper/scorer registry resolution, provider capability vetoes, ...) are carried by the conformance corpus manifest. These artefacts are family engineering infrastructure — schemas the implementing frameworks conform to — not a standard for third-party implementations.

propertyNames.$comment: Part I, named path anchors (2026-07-29): root names match [a-z][a-z0-9-]*.

additionalProperties.$comment: Part I, named path anchors (2026-07-29): a relative directory path, resolved against the declaring file's directory. An absolute value is refused — absolute locations are the MAVAI_ROOT_<NAME> override's job (the POSIX spelling is schema-refused; loaders refuse every spelling).

roots.$comment: Part I, named path anchors (2026-07-29): the identical construct to the contract format's, stated once there (MAVAI-CONTRACT-FORMAT.md Part I, named path anchors); roots are per-file, never shared between a contract file and its services file. Reference resolution, undeclared-reference and dead-declaration refusals, directory existence, and the override are loader obligations (semantic, manifest-carried).

systemPromptValue.$comment: SII.3, named-path-anchors amendment (2026-07-29): an inline string, or {file: <path>} — the referenced file decoded as UTF-8 text, the path resolving relative to this file's directory or against a declared root; the resolved string is the covariate exactly as if written inline (resolved-as-used, SII.4; fingerprint law, SII.6).

scalarValue.$comment: SII.7: configuration values are scalars (string, number, boolean) — matching the mavai-explore-1 factors value space.

type.$comment: SII.7: names a service implementation in the type registry — a built-in (language-model) or a user type registered in host code. Registry resolution is semantic, manifest-carried.

configuration.$comment: Part I: exactly one configuration: block — the complete set of covariate values the service runs under; no parameter lives anywhere else in the definition (the uniformity rule).

explorations.$comment: Part I / SII.6: builder-style entries, each declaring only the covariates that deviate from the baseline record. An entry restating the baseline (including an empty entry) is refused — duplicate resolved grid points are semantic, manifest-carried.

optimizations.$comment: Part I (amendment 2026-07-25): a non-empty list of optimize-experiment entries, consumed only by the optimize verb — measure, test, and explore never read it.

configuration.$comment: SII.7: for a user-registered type the factory's signature is the configuration schema (validated by the reader at load time, not expressible here); values are scalars.

id.$comment: Part I (amendment 2026-07-25): names the run and its artefact — letters, digits, dots, underscores, hyphens. Required when the definition declares more than one entry, and unique within it — both semantic, manifest-carried.

stepper.$comment: Part I: the registered name of the algorithm proposing each next configuration. Registry resolution is semantic, manifest-carried.

stepper-config.$comment: Part I: bound against the stepper factory's signature — the factory's signature is the schema (SII.7 discipline), validated by the reader at load time, not expressible here.

scorer.$comment: Part I: the registered scorer judging an iteration; default pass-rate.

max-iterations.$comment: Part I: required — the cap always bounds the spend.

no-improvement-window.$comment: Part I: plateau detection; a window the cap can never let fire is advisory-noted, not refused.

initial.$comment: Part I: iteration 0's configuration replacements, with an exploration entry's overlay semantics; an overlay restating the baseline is refused — semantic, manifest-carried.

system-prompt.$comment: SII.3: required — the system prompt is what turns a model into a service, the defining covariate of a language-model-backed service; a configuration without one is refused. An inline string, or {file: <path>} (named-path-anchors amendment, 2026-07-29).

provider.$comment: SII.3: the named vendor integrations; omitted means the generic OpenAI-compatible protocol against the environment-configured endpoint.

model.$comment: SII.3: optional, with an environment default.

top-p.$comment: SII.3, client-factors amendment 2026-07-17: a number in (0, 1], the nucleus-sampling mass.

thinking.$comment: SII.3, client-factors amendment 2026-07-17: default none. Provider vetoes (anthropic's thinking/sampling exclusion) are semantic, manifest-carried.

prompt-caching.$comment: SII.3, client-factors amendment 2026-07-17: default false; correctness-invariant by construction, stochastic impact confined to latency and cost.

max-tokens.$comment: SII.3 (adopted 2026-07-25): the output-token ceiling — a distributional factor, fingerprinted; unstated means the format-normative default 4096.

deadline-ms.$comment: SII.3 (adopted 2026-08-07): how long the reader waits for one response before recording a failed delivery, in whole milliseconds — bounding the whole exchange, not the connection. A distributional factor, fingerprinted. No upper bound is stated here: patience is the author's to spend, and the rule the format enforces is that a reader ships a finite default and records it resolved, never that the number is small.

response-schema.$comment: SII.3: an inline mapping — the JSON Schema the model is instructed to satisfy, passed through the provider's structured-output mechanism; a covariate unconditionally (the generation-side rule, 2026-07-17). Per-provider support is a load-time refusal, semantic, manifest-carried.

capabilities.$comment: SII.3 (amendment 2026-07-25): the author-declared capability allowance — a closed set; the per-modality media capabilities gate the encoding of file-sourced input parts (an undeclared capability is never sent silently). Adapter-encodability refusals are semantic, manifest-carried; the allowance is fingerprinted into provenance.

languageModelConfiguration.$comment: SII.3: the type: language-model configuration block holds every parameter; no parameter may appear outside it. Token-related parameters are deliberately absent from v0. Secrets never appear in this file — credentials are environment-only.

languageModelDelta.$comment: Part I / SII.6: a partial language-model configuration — an exploration entry's deviations, or an optimization entry's initial: overlay — the same key vocabulary, nothing required.
